clue.text: Musical instrument Rob heard

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the sound of the word for rob, not its spelling

parts.note: to rob is to loot

explanation.surface: A thief makes off with someone's instrument, and it is overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute is a plucked string instrument with a rounded back, popular in Renaissance music.

clue.text: Unwind the flexes with plug in

indicators.note: flexes means bends, so the letters of the and plug in are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Electrical cables with a plug fitted, and a cue to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexes' looks like a noun (electric cables, in British usage) but is the verb bend, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten up is to relax and stop being so serious, which is to unwind.

clue.text: Beat with pizzazz for dance

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
go means energy and dash, pizzazz

explanation.surface: Keeping the beat with flair is what dancing needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a dramatic ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Your compiler is offensive but cool

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself says I am, shortened to I'M
personal remarks are offensive ones aimed at someone

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being rude yet unflustered.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool manner is distant and detached, lacking warmth, which is what impersonal means.

clue.text: River rising above Hebrew character in drama

indicators.note: above places the reversed river before the letter in a down answer
rising in a down clue means the river's name reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
beth is the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet

explanation.surface: A river climbs above a Hebrew letter in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns CAM into MAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is Shakespeare's tragedy, a play and so a drama.

clue.text: City on theme having taken abnormal position

indicators.note: on places the city letters on top of the theme word in a down answer

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
a theme is a topic

explanation.surface: A city sits on a subject that has gone off course.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine an ectopic organ or pregnancy is one found away from its normal site.

clue.text: Gascoyne-Cecil unambiguous where 14 monuments located

parts.note: Robert Gascoyne-Cecil, Marquess of Salisbury, was a Victorian British Prime Minister
plain means clear and unambiguous

explanation.surface: A clear statement from a statesman about where old monuments stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The 14 is NEOLITHIC, 14 across: Stonehenge and other Stone Age monuments stand on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Salisbury Plain is the chalk plateau holding Stonehenge and many prehistoric burial mounds.

clue.text: Big cheese sandwich endlessly seen in menu terribly old

indicators.note: seen in means the trimmed sandwich word appears inside the other pieces
terribly means badly done, so the letters of menu are muddled
endlessly means the word for sandwich loses its last letter

parts.note: a round is a sandwich made from two slices of bread

explanation.surface: An important person spots a sandwich on an awful old menu.
explanation.walkthrough: A round is a British term for a sandwich made from two slices of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Numero uno, Italian for number one, is the top person, as is the big cheese.

clue.text: Boisterous males casing knight's estate

indicators.note: casing means the lads letters enclose the knight letter like a case

parts.note: lads are young men, typically rowdy ones
N is the chess abbreviation for knight; the 's merely links

explanation.surface: Rowdy young men surround a knight's property.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large area of property, and lands means such holdings of ground.

clue.text: Transporting heavy weight, sends giants to move megaliths

indicators.note: transporting means carrying, so the jumbled letters carry the weight word inside them
to move means the letters of sends giants are shifted around

parts.note: a ton is a heavy unit of weight

explanation.surface: Giants are dispatched to haul huge stones into place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges SENDS GIANTS into STANDINGSES, and TON is carried inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Megaliths are large prehistoric stones set upright, also called standing stones.

clue.text: Hereditary information overturning quote

parts.note: gen is slang for information

indicators.note: overturning means the word for quote is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it

explanation.surface: Inherited data is being cited the wrong way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturning' turns CITE into ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic traits are passed down through the genes, so they are hereditary.

clue.text: Argonaut crew on for crossing lake

indicators.note: crossing means the team-and-on letters straddle the lake abbreviation, which sits inside them

parts.note: a crew is a team

explanation.surface: An Argonaut's crew sail on across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Telamon, father of Ajax, sailed with Jason on the Argo in Greek myth, making him one of the Argonauts.

clue.text: Through Newcastle locally river finds course

indicators.note: through means the river letter runs through the middle of the local name

parts.note: Geordies call Newcastle the Toon, as in the football club's Toon Army

explanation.surface: A river flows through Newcastle and finds its course.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Troon is a championship golf course on the Ayrshire coast in Scotland, so 'course' is the golf sense, not a river's course.
explanation.definitionFit: Troon is a famous Scottish links that hosts the Open Championship, a golf course by name.

clue.text: Former pseuds delaying European revelations

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: delaying means the European letter is pushed later in the word for pseuds

parts.note: pseuds are pretentious people, poseurs

explanation.surface: Old show-offs are slow to reveal Europe's secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delaying' moves the E of POSEURS later, giving POSURES.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposures are disclosures of hidden wrongdoing, which is what revelations about someone are.

clue.text: Of a certain age, one Dotty settled here in Rome

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters of one are scrambled

parts.note: a bird that has settled has lit on a branch
hic is the Latin word for here, the language of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A slightly mad woman named Dotty has made her home in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' rearranges ONE into NEO. 'Of a certain age' usually means middle-aged; here it is the New Stone Age.
explanation.definitionFit: Neolithic describes the New Stone Age, a particular period of prehistory, hence belonging to a certain age.

clue.text: Those always having potential to rekindle relationships?

definitions.text: Those always having potential to rekindle relationships?

parts.words: Those always having potential to rekindle relationships?
parts.note: former partners may revive a romance, and the word for a romance plays on fire that could be rekindled

explanation.surface: People who might always revive a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rekindle' leans on the fire image: a former sweetheart is a flame that once burned and might again.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former lover, someone with whom romance could flare up anew.

clue.text: USP used around ancient city as appropriate

indicators.note: used around means the given letters are wrapped around the ancient city

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A unique selling point is borrowed for an old city as seems fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective (suitable) but is the verb: to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp something is to seize it without right, the same as to appropriate it.

clue.text: Beyond nervous — possibly frightened or terrified?

parts.note: past means beyond, as in past the station
tense means nervous

explanation.surface: Someone more than nervous, perhaps scared or terrified.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a state of mind; the definition is grammatical: 'frightened' and 'terrified' are verbs in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightened and terrified are past forms of verbs, examples of the past tense.

clue.text: Greedy gobbler outside party an Asian stray

indicators.note: outside means the pig letters go round the party word

parts.note: a greedy eater is called a pig
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A greedy eater is kept outside a party for an ownerless Asian animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pi-dog, or pye-dog, is a half-wild ownerless dog roaming villages in South Asia.

clue.text: On my back in a sense unknown

indicators.note: in means the first pieces are placed inside the a-plus-sense letters

parts.note: nous is common sense
taken as written

indicators.note: back means the word my is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something sensed on one's back remains a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: Nous is British informal for common sense or gumption.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonymous writer or donor is one whose name is not known.

clue.text: Young forever, lacking regular income, wife must leave

indicators.note: must leave means the wife letter is removed

parts.note: someone without a wage is wageless

explanation.surface: Staying youthful, unpaid, and the wife has to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageless means never growing old, staying young eternally.

clue.text: Thrust forward, storming redoubt

indicators.note: storming means wildly disturbing, so the letters of redoubt are rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops push ahead, storming a fortification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storming' reads as attacking the redoubt, a small fort, but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to push something out or forward, especially unwelcome.

clue.text: Everything too much about blokes: share in growing concern

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: about means the too-much letters go round the word for blokes

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, too much
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Everything is excessive with men around; there's a stake in a thriving business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing concern' plays on 'going concern': an allotment is a plot where vegetables grow. In Britain councils rent these small garden plots to residents.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is both a share allotted to someone and a rented plot for growing vegetables.

clue.text: Answer bugs Professor Roberts for example

parts.note: lice are small bugs

explanation.surface: A response that irritates a professor.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice Roberts is a British anatomist, professor and television presenter; 'bugs' looks like a verb (annoys) but gives insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is the first name of Professor Alice Roberts, so she is an example of an Alice.

clue.text: Escape quickly authorised?

definitions.meaning: ..., short for legitimate, means allowed or authorised

explanation.surface: Is getting away fast allowed?
explanation.definitionFit: Leg it is slang for running off, and legit is informal for lawful or sanctioned.

clue.text: Good media personality shows spirit

parts.note: a host presents a TV or radio show

explanation.surface: A decent broadcaster displays plenty of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is the spirit of a dead person.

clue.text: Huge mass seen twice in turbulent Seine

indicators.note: in means the doubled mass letters go inside the scrambled river name
turbulent water is churned up, so the letters of Seine are mixed

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
seen twice means the M for mass appears a second time

explanation.surface: A great mass seen in the rough waters of the Seine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges SEINE into IENSE, and the doubled M goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means extremely large, a straightforward synonym for huge.

clue.text: Nuncio nuts about rook as mythical creature

indicators.note: about means the jumbled nuncio letters wrap round the rook letter
nuts means crazy, so the letters of nuncio are jumbled

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A papal envoy goes mad about a chess piece, as if it were a mythical beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges NUNCIO into UNICON; 'about' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a legendary horse with a single horn, a beast of myth.

clue.text: Area down a lot makes changes to use assets before vote

indicators.note: changes to means the letters of use assets are altered into a new order

parts.note: X is the cross marked on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: Someone a lot down on their luck reshuffles their assets before a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: East Sussex is an English county crossed by the South Downs, chalk hills, so it is 'down' a lot. 'changes to' rearranges USE ASSETS into EASTSUSSE.
explanation.definitionFit: East Sussex is a county on England's south coast largely covered by the South Downs hills.

clue.text: Viewer's sore as regularly sat by set?

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of sat by set, starting from the first

explanation.surface: Someone sat by the television set gets sore eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: A viewer here is an eye, the organ you view with.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a sore on the eye.
